title: NULL values, calculations, AS
explanation: Welcome to Level 2! Remember NULL from Lesson 0? It means a value is missing. NULL is tricky: you can't find it with = NULL. Instead, use IS NULL to find missing values, and IS NOT NULL to find values that exist. You can also do math in SQL with + (add), - (subtract), * (multiply), and / (divide). When you make a new column with math, give it a nickname with AS, so it has a clear name in your results.

lines.line: SELECT title, price, price * 2 AS two_copies
lines.explain: Show the title and price, plus a new column: the price times 2, nicknamed two_copies.
Only keep games that have a rating. Games with a missing (NULL) rating are filtered out.

tasks.prompt: Show the title of every game that has no rating.
tasks.answer: SELECT title FROM games WHERE rating IS NULL;
hints: A missing value is NULL. Remember, = NULL doesn't work.

solution_lines.explain: Keep only games where the rating is missing.

tasks.prompt: Show the title and rating of every game that DOES have a rating.
tasks.answer: SELECT title, rating FROM games WHERE rating IS NOT NULL;
hints: This is the opposite of the last task.

solution_lines.explain: Show me the title and rating columns.
Keep only games where the rating is not missing.

tasks.prompt: Show the title of every game, plus how old it is in 2026. Name that new column age.
tasks.answer: SELECT title, 2026 - release_year AS age FROM games;
hints: How old is a game? Subtract its release year from 2026.

solution_lines.explain: Show the title, plus a new column: 2026 minus the release year, nicknamed age.

tasks.prompt: Show the title and age (in 2026) of games older than 10 years, oldest first.
tasks.answer: SELECT title, 2026 - release_year AS age FROM games WHERE 2026 - release_year > 10 ORDER BY age DESC;
hints: Use the same age calculation in your WHERE line, then sort it from Lesson 3.
WHERE 2026 - release_year > 10 ORDER BY age DESC

solution_lines.explain: Show the title and the age of each game.
Keep games where the age is more than 10.
Sort by age, oldest first. You can sort by a nickname you made with AS.

tasks.prompt: Predict first: how many rows will this return?
tasks.code: SELECT title FROM games WHERE rating < 9;
hints: Look at the rating column. What happens to the games with a NULL rating?
A missing value isn't less than 9, or more than 9. NULL rows never match a comparison, so they're left out.

solution_lines.explain: Keep games rated under 9: Fortnite, Stardew Valley, Among Us, and League of Legends. The two NULL ratings are skipped, because missing isn't a number.

recap: You just learned to find missing values with IS NULL and IS NOT NULL, do math in your queries, and name new columns with AS. Bonus: NULL never matches a comparison like < or >.
